name: Glyoxylate Metabolism
notes: Collection of glyoxylate-related pathways including BHAC cycle and other glyoxylate assimilation/conversion pathways.

nodes.name: BHAC transcriptional regulator
nodes.notes: Transcriptional regulator for bhcABCD operon. Not required for catalytic activity.

nodes.name: β-hydroxyaspartate aldolase
nodes.notes: Aldolase that condenses glycine and glyoxylate to form β-hydroxyaspartate. First glyoxylate incorporation step.

nodes.name: β-hydroxyaspartate dehydratase
nodes.notes: Dehydratase that converts β-hydroxyaspartate to iminosuccinate.

nodes.name: iminosuccinate reductase
nodes.notes: NADH-dependent reductase that converts iminosuccinate to L-aspartate.

nodes.name: aspartate-glyoxylate aminotransferase
nodes.notes: PLP-dependent aminotransferase that converts L-aspartate to oxaloacetate while regenerating glycine from glyoxylate. Second glyoxylate incorporation and glycine regeneration step. Note: BLAST reference has typo 'bhaA' instead of 'bhcA'.

nodes.name: isocitrate lyase
nodes.notes: Isocitrate lyase - key enzyme of glyoxylate shunt. Cleaves isocitrate to succinate and glyoxylate, bypassing CO2-releasing steps of TCA cycle. Essential for growth on acetate and fatty acids.

nodes.name: malate synthase
nodes.notes: Malate synthase - condenses acetyl-CoA with glyoxylate to form malate. Second essential enzyme of glyoxylate shunt. Also known as glcB in some organisms.

nodes.name: tartronate-semialdehyde synthase
nodes.notes: Glyoxylate carboligase - catalyzes dimerization of two glyoxylate molecules to form tartronate semialdehyde. First step of glycerate pathway for glyoxylate assimilation.

nodes.name: tartronate-semialdehyde reductase
nodes.notes: Tartronate-semialdehyde reductase - reduces tartronate semialdehyde to D-glycerate. Second step of glycerate pathway.

nodes.name: glycerate 2-kinase
nodes.notes: Glycerate kinase - phosphorylates D-glycerate to 2-phosphoglycerate, linking to glycolysis. Also known as garK. Third step of glycerate pathway.

nodes.name: glycolate oxidase complex
nodes.notes: Glycolate oxidase complex - three-subunit enzyme that oxidizes glycolate to glyoxylate. glcD (FAD-binding), glcE (iron-sulfur), glcF (cytochrome) all required for activity.

nodes.name: glycolate permease
nodes.notes: Glycolate permease - imports glycolate from external environment. Similar to L-lactate permease. Provides substrate for glycolate oxidase pathway.

nodes.name: L-lactate permease
nodes.notes: L-lactate permease - primarily transports L-lactate but can also transport glycolate. Alternative to glcA for glycolate uptake. Multiple KO IDs represent different lactate permease variants (lldP, lctP, lutP).

nodes.name: phosphoglycolate phosphatase
nodes.notes: Phosphoglycolate phosphatase - converts 2-phosphoglycolate to glycolate. Important for salvaging phosphoglycolate produced by RuBisCO oxygenase activity (photorespiration).

nodes.name: glyoxylate reductase
nodes.notes: Glyoxylate/hydroxypyruvate reductase - NADH-dependent reduction of glyoxylate to glycolate. Alternative to glycerate pathway for glyoxylate detoxification.

nodes.name: glyoxylate/hydroxypyruvate reductase
nodes.notes: Glyoxylate/hydroxypyruvate reductase - NADPH-dependent alternative to ghrA. Can reduce both glyoxylate and hydroxypyruvate.

nodes.name: acetyl-CoA C-acetyltransferase
nodes.notes: Acetyl-CoA C-acetyltransferase - condenses two acetyl-CoA to acetoacetyl-CoA. First step of ethylmalonyl-CoA pathway upper branch. Also involved in many other CoA metabolism pathways.

nodes.name: acetoacetyl-CoA reductase
nodes.notes: Acetoacetyl-CoA reductase - reduces acetoacetyl-CoA to 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA. Second step of EMC pathway upper branch.

nodes.name: 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydratase
nodes.notes: 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydratase - converts 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA to crotonyl-CoA. Third step of EMC pathway upper branch.

nodes.name: crotonyl-CoA carboxylase/reductase
nodes.notes: Crotonyl-CoA carboxylase/reductase - carboxylates and reduces crotonyl-CoA to ethylmalonyl-CoA. Key enzyme of EMC pathway. Diagnostic marker for this pathway.

nodes.name: ethylmalonyl-CoA mutase
nodes.notes: Ethylmalonyl-CoA mutase - isomerizes ethylmalonyl-CoA to methylsuccinyl-CoA. Diagnostic enzyme of EMC pathway. Branching point for lower branches.

nodes.name: (2S)-methylsuccinyl-CoA dehydrogenase
nodes.notes: Methylsuccinyl-CoA dehydrogenase - converts methylsuccinyl-CoA to methylfumaryl-CoA. Step in EMC pathway upper branch leading to malyl-CoA cleavage.

nodes.name: 2-methylfumaryl-CoA hydratase
nodes.notes: 2-methylfumaryl-CoA hydratase - converts methylfumaryl-CoA to malyl-CoA. Also listed as mcd in some databases. Penultimate step before malyl-CoA cleavage.

nodes.name: malyl-CoA/(S)-citramalyl-CoA lyase
nodes.notes: Malyl-CoA lyase - cleaves malyl-CoA to acetyl-CoA and glyoxylate (upper branch) or acts on citramalyl-CoA. Key branch point enzyme.

nodes.name: (3S)-malyl-CoA thioesterase
nodes.notes: Malyl-CoA thioesterase - alternative to mcl lyase activity. Hydrolyzes malyl-CoA to malate (lower-malate branch). Diagnostic for malate-producing variant.

nodes.name: propionyl-CoA carboxylase complex
nodes.notes: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase complex - biotin-dependent carboxylase with two subunits (pccA alpha, pccB beta). Both subunits required for activity. Converts propionyl-CoA to methylmalonyl-CoA.

nodes.name: methylmalonyl-CoA/ethylmalonyl-CoA epimerase
nodes.notes: Methylmalonyl-CoA epimerase - interconverts R and S stereoisomers of methylmalonyl-CoA. Required for both EMC pathway and propionate metabolism.

nodes.name: methylmalonyl-CoA mutase
nodes.notes: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase - converts methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA (lower-succinyl-CoA branch). B12-dependent enzyme. Links to TCA cycle.

bhac_cycle.name: β-Hydroxyaspartate Cycle (BHAC)
bhac_cycle.source: KEGG map00630, Schada von Borzyskowski et al. 2019 (doi:10.1038/s41586-019-1748-4)
bhac_cycle.notes: Marine proteobacterial pathway for glyoxylate assimilation via β-hydroxyaspartate cycle. Net reaction: 2 Glyoxylate + NADH → Oxaloacetate + NAD+ + H2O. Glycine is a cyclic intermediate regenerated by bhcA. Complete BHAC cycle for glyoxylate assimilation.

edges.notes: Glycine is regenerated by bhcA and recycled back to bhcC. This closes the cycle. Non-structural edge - excluded from DAG validation to avoid false cycle error, but shown in visualizations.

scoring.notes: All four catalytic genes (bhcA, bhcB, bhcC, bhcD) are required for cycle completion. bhcR is regulatory and optional. Strict threshold since no partial functionality possible.

glyoxylate_shunt.name: Glyoxylate Shunt / Glyoxylate Cycle
glyoxylate_shunt.notes: Classic glyoxylate shunt that bypasses CO2-releasing steps of TCA cycle. Enables growth on C2 compounds (acetate, fatty acids) by conserving carbon. aceA cleaves isocitrate to succinate + glyoxylate, aceB condenses glyoxylate + acetyl-CoA to malate.

edges.notes: Succinate byproduct enters TCA cycle. Not part of glyoxylate shunt flow but important for carbon balance.
Acetyl-CoA from fatty acid oxidation or acetate uptake. External substrate required for malate synthase.

scoring.notes: Both genes are essential and diagnostic for glyoxylate shunt. Strict 1.0 threshold - no partial functionality.

glycerate_pathway.name: Glycerate Pathway (Tartronate Semialdehyde Pathway)
glycerate_pathway.notes: Alternative glyoxylate assimilation pathway via tartronate semialdehyde and D-glycerate. Net reaction: 2 Glyoxylate + NADH + ATP → 2-Phosphoglycerate (feeds into glycolysis). Independent of both BHAC and glyoxylate shunt - provides different route for glyoxylate detoxification and carbon assimilation.

scoring.notes: All three genes required for complete pathway. gcl is highly diagnostic - glyoxylate carboligase is specific to this pathway.

glycolate_oxidase.name: Glycolate Oxidase Pathway
glycolate_oxidase.notes: Glycolate oxidation to glyoxylate via glcDEF complex. Provides glyoxylate substrate for other pathways (BHAC, glyoxylate shunt, glycerate pathway). Important feeder pathway - organisms with glycolate oxidase can utilize external glycolate as carbon source.

scoring.notes: Single complex node with three required subunits (glcD, glcE, glcF - all KOs must be found). Not pathway-specific (glycolate oxidase found in many contexts), so no marker gene defined.

glycolate_transport.name: Glycolate Transport
glycolate_transport.notes: Glycolate permease imports glycolate from external environment. Provides substrate for glycolate oxidase pathway. Transport alone doesn't indicate glyoxylate metabolism - must be interpreted with downstream pathways. Both glcA (glycolate-specific) and lldP (L-lactate permease with glycolate activity) can transport glycolate.

scoring.notes: glcA and lldP are alternatives - only one needed for glycolate transport. Not diagnostic alone - only meaningful if glycolate oxidase or other downstream pathways present.

phosphoglycolate_pathway.name: Phosphoglycolate to Glyoxylate Pathway
phosphoglycolate_pathway.notes: Two related detoxification activities: (1) PGP dephosphorylates 2-phosphoglycolate to glycolate (photorespiration salvage), (2) ghrA/ghrB reduce glyoxylate to glycolate (glyoxylate detoxification). These are independent reactions, not a connected pathway - both produce glycolate but from different toxic substrates.

edges.notes: ghrA reduces glyoxylate (from external sources or other pathways) to glycolate
ghrB reduces glyoxylate (from external sources or other pathways) to glycolate

scoring.notes: PGP is essential. ghrA and ghrB are alternatives - only one needed. Lower threshold since glyoxylate reductases have broad substrate specificity. Not pathway-specific - involved in photorespiration salvage.

ethylmalonyl_coa.name: Ethylmalonyl-CoA Pathway
ethylmalonyl_coa.notes: Complete ethylmalonyl-CoA pathway for C2 (acetyl-CoA) assimilation with two terminal branches at malyl-CoA. Main trunk: 2 acetyl-CoA → ethylmalonyl-CoA → methylsuccinyl-CoA → malyl-CoA. Terminal branches: (A) mcl cleaves malyl-CoA to acetyl-CoA + glyoxylate (producing propionyl-CoA which continues via pccAB → epi → MUT → succinyl-CoA), (B) mcl2 hydrolyzes malyl-CoA to malate. Found in Methylobacterium and marine Rhodobacterales. Organisms use different branch combinations depending on metabolic needs.

edges.notes: Acetyl-CoA product of mcl cleavage - recycled into other pathways
Glyoxylate product of mcl cleavage - recycled into other pathways
Terminal product of pccAB branch, feeds TCA cycle

output.notes: Three alternative outputs: acetyl-CoA + glyoxylate (mcl), malate (mcl2), or succinyl-CoA (MUT)

scoring.notes: Main trunk (atoB through mch) required. Terminal branches are alternatives - organism needs at least ONE of: mcl, mcl2, or pccAB/epi/MUT. ccr and ecm are highly diagnostic markers. 7/10 threshold allows for missing terminal branch genes.
